Hi Aisha — appreciate the detail and the token export. Quick notes on options and ballpark unit economics so you have context while finance reviews:

1) Licensing models (private/VPC):
   - Annual license + variable usage: annual platform license (covers runtime + control plane) + usage invoiced monthly. This tends to have higher $/1M tokens at low volume but less upfront infra commitment.
   - Committed (reserved) capacity: you reserve GPU capacity (monthly/annual commit) with a much lower blended $/1M token rate; ideal if you have predictable growth (your 3–10B/mo band looks good for this).
   - Per-environment add-ons: base license includes 1 prod + 1 staging; additional envs and replica regions billed as fixed add-ons.

2) Support tiers (high level):
   - Standard: business-hours support, 24–48h P1 response.
   - Premium: 24/7 incident response, <1h P1, access to priority escalation and quarterly runbooks.
   - Enterprise: Premium + designated TAM, scheduled quarterly reviews and custom SLAs.

3) Rough unit economics (blended, indicative):
   - Committed reserved capacity: ~"$450–$700" per 1M tokens (volume-dependent, bands apply).
   - Annual license + variable usage: ~"$800–$1,200" per 1M tokens at your starting scale.
   - Hosted API (for reference): ~"$1,200–$2,000" per 1M tokens depending on model — private gives you control and predictable performance but requires licensing/infra costs.

4) Environment pricing: base license covers 1 prod + 1 staging; additional envs (dev/DR/replica) ~ $15k–$25k/yr each depending on size and isolation needs.

I’m attaching a one-pager (cheatsheet) with these bands and the assumptions used to compute $/1M tokens. If your budget target is $750–$1,000/1M, the annual license + variable option maps close to the top end of that band at your current volume; if you expect to be at 3B+/mo within 6–12 months the committed model will get you into the $450–$700 band.

Next step: with your permission I’ll loop in our finance lead and solutions engineering (Dev) to build a formal quote (line items: license, reserved infra vs usage, env add-ons, premium support). Any procurement constraints (PO terms, payment cadence, procurement contact) we should know about?

Best,
Ben

(Internal SE note — keeping the thread so FintechCo sees the context)

Couple of technical/ops clarifications to include in the proposal:
- Token accounting: we should propose a daily token reconciliation and a reserve buffer for peak windows (we can offer burst buckets on top of committed capacity).
- Quantization/throughput profile: for fraud assistant workloads we can expect ~25–40 tokens/sec per GPU depending on model and sequence length; this affects how many GPUs to reserve for a given tokens/month target.
- Replica/DR: if they require cross-region replica for geo-failover, price as a smaller fixed infra add-on but note network egress could be incremental.

I’ll draft the GPU sizing assumptions and a sample commit table (bands: 1B–3B, 3B–6B, 6B+). Once Ben gets confirmation on the budget band, I can produce the committed-capacity SKU lines for the quote.

—Dev
